title: Sincerity and compassion
intro: Doing good only for Allah, and feeling for others in their troubles.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Have you seen the one who denies the Judgement? That is the one who harshly drives away the orphan and does not encourage feeding the poor. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Ma‘un 107:1–3)</small>
Sincerity is a basic quality of every Muslim: showing faith and doing good only for Allah’s pleasure. Only deeds done sincerely for Allah are accepted and rewarded.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: O believers, be mindful of Allah and be with the truthful. <small>(Qur’an, At-Tawbah 9:119)</small> And they were commanded only to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Bayyinah 98:5)</small>

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “Tell the truth, for truth leads to goodness, and goodness leads to Jannah. A person keeps telling the truth until he is written with Allah as truthful…” (Muslim)

Islam teaches us to be sincere with ourselves and others, and to tell the truth even when it is against us. Sincerity means telling the truth, keeping promises, doing what we took on, sincere deeds and honest work. It is the opposite of lying, cheating, short-changing and two-facedness. The Prophet (SAW) said: “Whoever does a deed so people hear of it, Allah will let it be heard; whoever does a deed so people see it, Allah will let it be seen.” (Bukhari and Muslim) So a deed done sincerely for Allah has a reward; a deed done only to be seen has none.

Compassion is feeling for someone in their trouble, suffering or problems. It makes us more caring and leads us to take real steps to help. Sometimes what a person in trouble needs most is someone to listen kindly, understand and comfort them.

Muhammad (SAW) was especially compassionate to the poor, the weak, the helpless and especially orphans. He said: “I and the one who looks after an orphan will be like this in Jannah,” showing his index and middle fingers together. (Bukhari) The companions asked: “Who is the best Muslim?” He said: “The one from whose tongue and hands other Muslims are safe.” (Bukhari)

learn.title: ‘Umar (RA) keeps watch
learn.html: It is told that the caliph ‘Umar (RA) passed by a group of travellers who had fallen asleep in the open after a long journey. Afraid someone might rob them, he stayed awake guarding them. ‘Amr ibn al-‘As asked why, and when he heard, he joined him – and both kept watch until dawn.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: “You see the believers in their love, mercy and kindness to each other like one body: when one part hurts, the whole body feels fever and sleeplessness.” (Bukhari)

items: offering condolence to a family when someone dies
being kind to orphans and looking after them
listening to someone who has problems

practice.title: Questions and task
prompts: 💬 What is sincerity? What is compassion, and why do we need it?

📋 Make a table – yes / no / sometimes: “I notice when someone isn’t feeling well”, “I like criticising others”, “I joke at others’ expense”, “I like talking to all my friends at maktab”. What does it show about your compassion?
